questions.question: Define scarcity.
questions.solution_html:
• Scarcity means the limited availability of resources compared to the unlimited wants
  • of people. It refers to the basic economic problem that resources are not sufficient
  • to satisfy all human wants.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What do you mean by Value Added in national accounting ?
questions.solution_html:
• Value added means the additional value created by a firm during the production
  • process. It is the difference between the value of the final output produced and the
  • cost of intermediate goods used.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is the difference between total utility and marginal utility?
questions.solution_html:
• Total utility refers to the overall satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a
  • given quantity of a good or service. Marginal utility is the additional satisfaction
  • that a consumer receives from consuming one additional unit of a good or service.
questions.final_answer: that a consumer receives from consuming one additional unit of a good or service
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Distinguish between productive and unproductive debt.
questions.solution_html:
• Productive debt refers to borrowing that is used for purposes which generate income
  • or create assets for the economy. for example, loans taken for irrigation projects, or
  • industries. Unproductive debt refers to borrowing used for purposes that do not
  • create income or assets for the economy. These debts do not contribute to economic
  • growth, for example, loans taken for war or government administrative expenses.
questions.final_answer: growth, for example, loans taken for war or government administrative expenses
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: State any two objectives of public expenditure.
questions.solution_html:
• To promote economic development: Government spends on infrastructure
  • education, health, and industries to improve the overall growth of the economy. To
  • ensure social welfare: Public expenditure aims to reduce poverty, provide basic
  • services, and improve the standard of living of the people.
questions.final_answer: services, and improve the standard of living of the people
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define Repo rate.

• Repo rate is the rate of interest at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends

questions.question: Differenciate commodity money and fiat money.
questions.solution_html:
• Commodity money is money that has its own intrinsic value. The material itself
  • (like gold, silver, or grains) has value even if it is not used as money. Fiat money is
  • money that has no intrinsic value but is accepted as money because the government
  • declares it as legal tender (like paper currency and coins).
questions.final_answer: declares it as legal tender (like paper currency and coins)

questions.question: Mention one function each of NABARD and MUDRA Bank.
questions.solution_html:
• NABARD provides refinancing facilities to banks and financial institutions for
  • promoting agriculture, rural industries, and overall rural development in the country.
  • MUDRA Bank provides credit support to micro and small enterprises by offering
  • loans under the Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun categories to promote entrepreneurship.
questions.final_answer: loans under the Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun categories to promote entrepreneurship
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define Primary Agricultural Credit Societies.
questions.solution_html:
• Primary Agricultural Credit Societies are village-level cooperative credit
  • institutions that provide short-term and medium-term loans to farmers for
  • agricultural and related activities. Value liberally

questions.question: How does MRS help in understanding consumer preferences between two / goods?
questions.solution_html:
• Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS) – helps in understanding consumer
  • preferences between two goods – shows how much of one good a consumer is
  • willing to give up to gain an extra unit of another – is measured as the slope of
  • the indifference curve – reflects the opportunity cost of choosing one good over
  • another – indicates the willingness to substitute one good for another while keeping
  • satisfaction constant – explains the trade-off and relative preference between the
  • two goods. Value liberally

questions.question: Describe the concept of non-tax revenue. Explain the primary sources of non- / tax revenue.
questions.solution_html:
• Non-tax revenue is income a government generates from sources other than taxes
  • Primary sources of non-tax revenue – fees and fines – penalties- escheats- special
  • assessment – dividends and profits from public sector undertakings- forfeitures
  • interest received on loans given to states and public enterprises.
questions.final_answer: interest received on loans given to states and public enterprises
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define monetary policy. Explain how it work as a credit comtrol tool?
questions.solution_html:
• Monetary policy – refers to the policy of the central bank to regulate money supply
  • credit, and interest rates in the economy – works as a credit control tool by
  • influencing the availability and cost of credit in the financial system –
  • uses quantitative measures like bank rate, repo rate, reverse repo rate, open market
  • operations, and cash reserve ratio( CRR), Statutory liquidity ratio (SLR)–
  • uses qualitative measures like moral suasion, credit rationing, margin requirements
  • consumer credit regulation, direct action selective credit control, and credit
  • rationing to influence the direction and quality of credit.
questions.final_answer: rationing to influence the direction and quality of credit
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: State the definitions of M0 and M1 compomemts of money supply. / Discuss the objectives, functions and importance of SIDBI in promoting small
questions.solution_html:
• Money supply – refers to the total stock of money available in an economy at a
  • particular time. Components- M0 – known as the reserve money – includes currency
  • in circulation + Bankers deposits with the RBI + Other deposits with the. M1 –
  • known as narrow money – includes currency with the public + demand deposits
  • with banks + and other deposits with the RBI.
questions.final_answer: with banks + and other deposits with the RBI
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What are the feautures of CBLO?
questions.solution_html:
• Features of CBLO – is a short
  • term money market instrument that allows borrowing and lending of funds against
  • collateral – operates through the Clearing Corporation of India Ltd
  • provides secured borrowing because transactions are backed by government
  • securities as collateral – offers flexible maturities – ensures anonymity of borrowers
  • and lenders- provides high liquidity.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the functions of Money market.
questions.solution_html:
• The money market is a market for short-term funds, which deals in financial assets
  • whose period of maturity is up to one year -It provides profitable short-term
  • investment opportunities for financial institutions – increases liquidity in the entire
  • economy – helps avoid wide seasonal fluctuations in interest rates – enables quick
  • transfer of funds across regions, preventing regional shortages and surpluses – offers
  • various credit instruments to augment the supply of short-term funds – supports the
  • effective implementation of central banking policies through a well-organised
  • structure.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
